page: Amazon Web Services m7gd.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by the 64-core AWS Graviton ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 processor. Operating at 2.6 GHz with dedicated single-threaded execution per core, the system bypasses hypervisor overhead entirely. It integrates 256 GB of DDR5 system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4 GB per core, along with 3800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage and 30 Gbps baseline networking throughput.

Benchmark results show notable strengths in parallel execution and memory subsystem throughput. In multi-core tests, the platform achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 21018.0 and a stress-ng score of 98066.33, both within the top tiers of measured hardware. Software compilation with Clang reaches 59722.0, placing in the top 10 percent, while DDR5 bandwidth reaches 254.06 GB/sec on uncached 256MB reads and 121.58 GB/sec on writes. However, single-threaded metrics remain within the average bracket, with Geekbench single-core at 1538.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 24.06 GB/sec.

The combination of 64 dedicated physical cores, massive local NVMe SSD capacity, and high DDR5 memory bandwidth delivers qualitative cost efficiency for scaled multi-threaded operations without virtualized resource contention. It is suited for demanding workloads including distributed caching layers, software compilation clusters, high-throughput static web serving, container orchestration, and localized relational or key-value databases requiring direct access to fast NVMe storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m7gd.metal is a bare-metal server built on the 64-core ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 architecture operating at 2.6 GHz without hyperthreading. It features 256 GB of DDR5 memory, 3800 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network throughput of 30 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier multi-threaded processing, software compilation speeds, and high memory bandwidth across large read and write workloads. Single-core execution and language model text generation metrics rank in the middle to lower tiers, reflecting an architecture prioritized for dense parallel scaling rather than extreme single-thread frequency. With direct hardware access, high memory throughput, and direct-attached NVMe storage, this server is configured for multi-threaded compilation pipelines, Redis caching clusters, high-concurrency web serving, and latency-sensitive database deployments.
